config.title: Design Auth Flow

intro.title: Design Auth Flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple authentication flow for a React application, allowing users to log in and log out. You will learn how to manage user authentication state using React's useState hook to track whether a user is signed in. The main technologies involved are React components, JSX for rendering, and event handlers to update the state based on user actions. By the end, you'll have a functional component that toggles between login and logout views, demonstrating a foundational pattern for handling user sessions in web apps.
intro.usecase: Authentication flows are essential in virtually every modern web application that requires user accounts. You'll implement this pattern in login screens for e-commerce sites like Amazon, social media platforms like Facebook, and productivity tools like Google Workspace. As a developer, you'll build these flows using protected routes, conditional rendering, and state management to control access to dashboards, user profiles, and premium content. Mastering auth flow design ensures you can create secure, professional applications that handle user sessions appropriately across different access levels.

objectives: Construct a React component to manage user authentication state
Implement form handling for login and registration inputs
Configure routing to protect private pages from unauthorized access
Integrate authentication state with conditional UI rendering
Initialize and manipulate user session data in local storage
Apply validation logic to user credentials before submission
Bind authentication events to appropriate UI components

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the AuthFlow component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthFlow that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named AuthFlow that returns null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the AuthFlow component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named AuthFlow is created and returns null.
successCriteria: The AuthFlow component is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component is named exactly 'AuthFlow' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a component named AuthFlow that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthFlow component, use useState to create an 'isLoggedIn' state variable initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with false as the initial value and destructure the returned array into two variables.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'isLoggedIn' that tracks whether the user is logged in, starting as false.
successCriteria: The AuthFlow component contains a useState call that declares 'isLoggedIn' initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've used useState correctly and named the variable 'isLoggedIn' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to call useState(false) and destructure it into [isLoggedIn, setIsLoggedIn] inside the component.

steps.title: Create login handler
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthFlow component, create a function named handleLogin that sets isLoggedIn to true and sets user to an object with name and email properties.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsLoggedIn with true and setUser with an object containing name and email strings.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleLogin function that updates both authentication states when called.
successCriteria: The handleLogin function is defined, calls setIsLoggedIn(true), and calls setUser with an object containing name and email properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it sets both isLoggedIn to true and user to an object with name and email.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleLogin function is missing or doesn't properly update both state values.

steps.title: Create logout handler
steps.instruction: Create a handleLogout function inside your component that sets isLoggedIn to false and user to null.
steps.hint: Define a function that updates both state variables to reflect a logged-out user.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a handleLogout function that will reset authentication state when called.
successCriteria: A handleLogout function is defined that calls setIsLoggedIn(false) and setUser(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the logout handler. Make sure it sets both isLoggedIn to false and user to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout handler is missing or doesn't properly reset the authentication state.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In your AuthFlow component's return statement, replace the current return value with a div element that has className 'auth-container' and contains an h1 element with the text 'Authentication Flow'.
steps.hint:
The return statement should look like: return (

Authentication Flow

);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic container structure with a heading, providing a foundation for the authentication flow UI.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div with className 'auth-container' and an h1 element with text 'Authentication Flow'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your return statement includes both the div with className 'auth-container' and the h1 with the exact text 'Authentication Flow'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement doesn't match the required structure. Check that you have a div with className 'auth-container' containing an h1 element.

steps.title: Display authentication status
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthFlow component's return statement, add a paragraph that conditionally displays 'Logged in: Yes' when isLoggedIn is true and 'Logged in: No' when false.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to check isLoggedIn and render different text accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element that shows 'Logged in: Yes' when the user is logged in and 'Logged in: No' when logged out.
successCriteria: The paragraph uses a ternary operator to conditionally render text based on the isLoggedIn state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using a ternary operator to check isLoggedIn and display the correct text for both true and false states.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph doesn't conditionally display the authentication status correctly. Review how to use ternary operators in JSX.

steps.title: Add login and logout buttons with handlers
steps.instruction: Add a login button that calls handleLogin when clicked and a logout button that calls handleLogout when clicked, conditionally showing only the relevant button based on isLoggedIn state.
steps.hint: Use conditional rendering with a ternary operator to show the login button when not logged in and the logout button when logged in. Remember to attach the onClick handlers to each button.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a login button when not logged in and a logout button when logged in, with each button wired to its respective handler.
successCriteria: Conditional rendering of login/logout buttons based on isLoggedIn state, with onClick handlers attached to handleLogin and handleLogout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both buttons are conditionally rendered based on isLoggedIn and have the correct onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly implemented. Check that you're using conditional rendering and that each button calls the correct handler function.
